CAP-011.notes: The current UI polls Core; no SSE/live-stream claim. Browser authorization uses HttpOnly device-session cookies and a readable CSRF cookie, never browser storage bearer tokens. QR pairing includes only a non-authorizing challenge identifier; phone sessions remain pending until owner approval and verification-code confirmation. The service worker is network-only and does not cache Core API responses or authorize offline work. Core reports CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, UNKNOWN or DISABLED from its private Office health projection; this does not prove mobile-network reachability. Overview, Decision Inbox, Action detail, the tabbed Campaign workspace, Runtime, Settings, Access & Devices, Agent Office and the read-only Issues snapshot foundation are implemented. Agent Office projects recorded participants only. Issues has an encrypted GitHub connection, one repository binding per Project, per-page ETag sync with credential-generation fencing and credential-wide backoff, stable issue identity and safe plain-text detail; governed intake, board ordering, Action/Campaign relationships, issue writing and a real authorized GitHub call remain later work. The Issues view is wired at /issues and component-tested; real browser acceptance remains pending. Unified intake now has a durable Project-scoped request, append-only pre-freeze operator messages, an explicit non-autonomous execution-policy grant, exact profile revision/plan-hash approval, and authoritative Lead withdrawal fencing. Assessment requires an authorized model gateway; no fixture fallback fabricates checks. A real Chromium journey now follows the ordinary intake path through Worker claim, exact candidate, independent verifier, semantic reviewer with model provenance, deterministic Quality Gate, changed files and Core-restart persistence using deterministic fixtures. Exact per-role routing is implemented: the frozen profile Lead route serves intake assessment, the frozen Semantic Reviewer route serves candidate review through candidate → Campaign → start evidence, and the implementer route remains the Campaign authorization route. A Codex App Server connection is executable for implementation but not one-shot assessment/review. Discovered-only model IDs depend on the current Core process discovery cache. Live provider inference, Compose acceptance for the intake path, aggregate token/cost accounting and independent acceptance remain unimplemented; these are displayed as explicit limits, not inferred state. The legacy Compose stack E2E passes. Docs remain a later slice. Decision Inbox now exposes only Core-backed actions with exact identity guards: approval of a frozen intake plan requires the exact plan hash/profile revision and explicit confirmation; ambiguous model reservations can be released; Lead withdrawal and Campaign cancellation require a reason and confirmation; every mutating action re-reads /office/decisions and aborts when the item revision changed or disappeared. Informational events remain separate and never render action controls. Full-scope Campaign authorization is not posted from the Inbox. Real browser acceptance for the new Inbox actions remains pending. Project onboarding now covers authorized GitHub repository listing and import through the existing encrypted connection, approved-root local import, human Project identity, a Core-backed summary and evidence-based manifest discovery. GitHub App/OAuth installation onboarding is not implemented; fine-grained tokens do not report OAuth scopes, and Office states no installation-wide access. Discovery evidence is advisory and never grants capabilities or check authority.

CAP-049.name: Operational Overview and Decision Inbox
CAP-049.job: See authoritative Core state, inspect blocked work and unresolved usage, and act only through explicit Core operations.
user_actions: inspect authorized campaigns, blocked work, decisions, measured spend, recent accepted candidates and recent events
separate action-required decisions from informational events and deep-link each item to its exact Project, Campaign, request, candidate or runtime object
approve an exact frozen intake plan only with its plan hash and profile revision, an explicit rationale and confirmation
resolve an AMBIGUOUS or UNKNOWN Core model call with an explicit operator reason
withdraw a frozen Lead request or cancel a Campaign with a reason and proportionate confirmation
inspect an Action frozen specification, checks and related Campaigns, Lead requests and delegations
CAP-049.notes: Overview and decisions are operator-authenticated Core projections; the client does not synthesize decisions. The Inbox exposes exact-revision intake approval, model-call resolution, Lead withdrawal, Campaign cancellation and navigation; every action revalidates the current decision revision, requires proportionate confirmation and is disabled while Core is unreachable. Full-scope Campaign authorization is not posted from the Inbox and links to the exact Campaign. Gate repair and provider-session termination remain outside the Inbox because no operator mutation is exposed. Component and Core projection tests cover the new actions; real browser acceptance remains pending. No SSE or live-stream claim.

CAP-050.notes: Campaign authorization, Run state, Attempt state and Gate outcome are displayed separately. The WorkGraph now includes a deterministic dependency layout, keyboard selection and a WorkUnit inspector while preserving the authoritative table. Graph presentation states are explicitly derived from recorded task status and dependencies; malformed data is surfaced, not repaired. Candidate diffs are bounded Core projections from the frozen base to the exact candidate commit/tree: changed-file status, additions/deletions, unified patches, binary/large/non-file omissions, file/patch/byte caps and exact candidate/Gate identity. GitHub pull request reads and actions use the encrypted Core connection; tokens stay server-side. Merge requires explicit confirmation and a fresh PR/check read, never bypasses GitHub branch protection and is never automatic. Real GitHub execution is NOT_TESTED until performed. Participant, tool-event and visual Office projections are provided by Agent Office.

CAP-051.name: Runtime operational console
CAP-051.job: Inspect Core health, registered Workers, provider sessions, model-call usage, reserved ceilings, cleanup, telemetry and runtime policy without terminal inspection.
user_actions: inspect Core health and registered Worker records
filter provider sessions by state usage cleanup worker or route
inspect recent and unresolved model-call reservations with measured usage and reservation ceiling
release an AMBIGUOUS or UNKNOWN reservation with an explicit audited reason
inspect telemetry export and semantic-review policy
CAP-051.notes: Sampled measured spend covers usage-known sessions and the latest 200 model calls. Reserved ceiling uses unresolved model-call max cost plus open provider-turn max cost. Unmeasured session count is shown separately; session cost is not claimed as a held ceiling. Supervisor, nested Podman and broker state are not exposed by the current Core API and are shown as unavailable, never inferred. Reservation release is explicit; no automatic release exists.

CAP-052.name: Provider and runtime Settings workspace
CAP-052.job: Configure Core-owned provider routes, credentials, models, limits and review policy while distinguishing configuration, connection testing and proven coding inference.
user_actions: inspect provider authentication status model endpoint auth modes and ChatGPT OAuth state
save or replace a provider credential without reading it back
revoke a credential after explicit consequence confirmation
set the default route and advanced token cost and rate limits
discover the real provider model catalog without claiming coding inference
enable or disable semantic review policy and inspect configuration audit history
CAP-052.notes: Credentials are encrypted at rest and never returned to the browser. A saved route is not proof of access. A connection test and model discovery read provider metadata only and are not coding inference. `GET /settings/providers/{provider}/models` returns a typed AVAILABLE or UNAVAILABLE catalog with a bounded model list, no proxy and no redirects; Codex App Server discovery is UNAVAILABLE by design. Discovery is an in-memory Core cache and is not persisted. ChatGPT OAuth remains visibly blocked or not applicable. Provider revisions do not rewrite frozen Campaign bindings.

CAP-054.name: Personal access and device sessions
CAP-054.job: Enroll a browser without a permanent API token, maintain independent device sessions, pair a phone with owner approval, and inspect optional private Tailscale access.
user_actions: complete first-run enrollment through the one-time local confirmation
inspect local and optional private remote access state
create a short-lived QR pairing challenge with a non-authorizing public identifier
compare verification codes and approve or reject a pending device
cancel an unclaimed or approved-awaiting-pickup challenge
revoke a single device, sign out the current device, or revoke all sessions
inspect bounded session and pairing security activity
CAP-054.notes: Session cookie material is HttpOnly. CSRF uses the dedicated readable SameSite cookie. Pairing challenge IDs do not grant authority and are stripped from browser history before phone requests. The phone receives a separate hashed poll capability, and Core creates a session only after the authenticated owner submits the matching code. The PWA service worker uses network-only requests; no offline authorization or sensitive-response caching is claimed. Access & Devices marks the current device, supports per-device and all-device revocation, shows bounded security activity, and cancels challenges explicitly. Tailscale status follows Core's private Office health probe and remains UNKNOWN when the probe is inconclusive. Author-run deterministic and real Chromium pairing evidence passed at implementation 9afbb6f; mobile-data Tailscale access, independent review and Product Owner approval remain pending.
